results.reason: Issue 1 states that the stock purchase is a Change of Control requiring Crestline's prior written consent under §15.4. It identifies the Disclosure Schedule's 'Notice only; no consent required' classification as wrong. It explains the resulting termination right and fee, and that the SPA §3.5 representation would be inaccurate, creating indemnity exposure.

Issue 7 notes only that Crestline may assign to an Affiliate or Qualified Transferee on notice without consent, and that this 'could also introduce a competitor of Varga.' It does not explain the §1.1 Qualified Transferee definition (any distributor of laboratory or diagnostic products in the Territory). It also does not say the definition fails to exclude Halvorsen's competitors.

Issue 6 explains that the First Amendment restates §12.3 so only §9 breaches are uncapped, dropping the §10 and §11 carve-outs. However, it never invokes the §17.5 order-of-precedence clause to explain why the amendment controls.
The response states that the original §12.3 excluded from the caps breaches of Sections 9 and 10 and indemnification obligations under Section 11.
The response states that §12.2 caps aggregate liability at amounts paid or payable to Supplier in the preceding 12 months.
The response is a formal memo with separately numbered issues. Each issue has 'Where it appears' (document and section), 'Why it matters', and 'Recommended fix' headings.
The response expressly concludes that consent, not merely notice, is required.
The response concludes that the §10 and §11 carve-outs were removed by the Amendment, so those claims are now capped.
